context: a letter from George Maw, which you are answering
exchanges:
Some months ago you asked me whether any examples of bud sports had come under my notice & think therefore you will like to have the accompanying fragment of a Fern-leaved Beech bearing a branch of the ordinary form of foliage   It is from the garden of Mr W De Crewdson of Helme Lodge Nr Kendal   The tree I am informed is about twenty years old, an occasional leaf of intermediate character occurs here & there, but for the most part the branches bearing the two forms are well marked & distinct.

Believe me Dr Sir | very truly yrs | George Maw

C Darwin Esq.

I am very much obliged to you for your great kindness in remembering my desire for information about sports, & for the curious & nicely dried specimen received yesterday. As it happens I have already seen this case, but I am not the less grateful to you for your kindness—

Pray believe me | Yours very faithfully | Ch. Darwin
